newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to return honour guard to Russia war tomb.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to return honour guard to Russia war tomb.

text.p: Goose-stepping soldiers will guard Moscow's tomb of the unknown soldier, but the Kremlin made clear on Wednesday that the ceremonial "honour guard number one" would not return to the tomb of Soviet State founder Vladimir Lenin.

"The president has made a decision in principle to restore the honour guards' Post Number One," Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference. "It will now be at the tomb of the unknown soldier."

President Boris Yeltsin, seeking a break with Soviet traditions, removed the honour guards at both the tomb of the unknown soldier and at Lenin's red marble mausoleum after he took power in the Kremlin, prompting fury from communists.
Lenin's tomb -- Post Number One -- had been the most prestigious place for the honour guard to serve.
Their precision march, a slow goose-step from the Kremlin gates to the doors of the mausoleum, was timed to the second.
The two-man guard changed as the clock on the Kremlin's Spassky Gate chimed the quarter-hour. Tourists watched, but photography was banned.
Yastrzhembsky made clear that Yeltsin's decision was timed to coincide with the anniversary of the allied victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two.
Victory Day, one of the most solemnly observed holidays in Russia, will be marked this year by the first Red Square military parade for five years.
